headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: transformers can write/run shells and browsers, while awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so prompt-injection and leakage are largely blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable with no I/O surfaces, while transformers exposes files, stdin/stdout, and APIs but there is no evidence it ingests awesome-selfhosted outputs by default. The pairwise injection path is therefore not established.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies awesome-selfhosted content into transformers stdin/stdout or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Require manual review before passing outputs between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces, while transformers can read/write files and call external APIs. Without a shared workspace or sensitive inputs, leakage is limited; the main risk appears only if the operator places sensitive files where transformers can access them.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in a shared directory readable by transformers, leakage risk increases.
IF transformers is pointed at secrets or regulated data, its broad egress can transmit them.
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside transformers' working directory.
Run transformers with a dedicated least-privilege account.
Block outbound network access for jobs that handle sensitive inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or execution capability, but transformers can execute shells, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files. If both are used in the same workspace, transformers can overwrite or alter artifacts that awesome-selfhosted indexes or references, creating a default conflict risk in shared directories.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF multiple transformers instances run concurrently without locking, race conditions can corrupt shared artifacts.
mitigations: Use file locks for any shared outputs.
Run only one transformers writer per workspace at a time.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge-management source, and transformers can render or act on its outputs via files or stdout. Because transformers has no documented verification gate here, any copied list entries or summaries may be treated as authoritative, so errors can cascade into downstream documents or actions.
conditions: IF awesome-selfhosted content is fed into transformers as instructions or facts, downstream errors can propagate.
IF transformers is used to generate reports from the list without human verification, mistaken entries can be published.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before publication.
Require source links for every derived claim.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable open-source list, and transformers is open-source document-processing software with no stated regulated-data handling in the profiles, so a compliance breach is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into transformers, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints, those must be checked separately.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into the pair.
Document the data classes allowed in transformers.
Review deployment policies before processing sensitive content.
